slides.2.title: 🏔️ Trentino-Alto Adige: Alpine Whites and Mountain Food
slides.2.content:
Alto Adige's distinctive Alpine terroir produces precisely aromatic, fresh, high-acid whites that pair superbly with the local, Austrian-influenced cooking. "What grows together goes together" is nowhere clearer than here.

🧀 Pinot Grigio / Gewürztraminer

South Tyrolean smoked ham (Speck): the fresh fruit of Alto Adige Pinot Grigio cuts through the smoky fat — an impeccable match from the same region.
Apple strudel: Gewürztraminer's lychee and rose echo the apple and cinnamon, a perfect application of the sweetness rule.
Alpine cheese (Graukäse): a mineral Pinot Grigio cleanly cuts through the cheese's fat.

🍷 Lagrein / Teroldego

Beef goulash: Lagrein's deep black fruit and violet perfectly suit stews influenced by the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
Venison: Teroldego's wild minerality naturally echoes game — Trentino's most local pairing.
Mushroom risotto: Lagrein's earthy base and the savoury mushrooms complement each other.

slides.3.title: 🌿 Friuli Venezia Giulia: Rich Whites and Cured Meats
slides.3.content:
Friuli is famous for some of Italy's finest whites — Friulano, Ribolla Gialla, Pinot Grigio — which pair superbly with the region's rich tradition of pork charcuterie and refined cooking.

🥩 Prosciutto di San Daniele

Friuli's proudest product, balanced between sweet and salty with delicate fat. Friulano (Tocai), with its almond and hay notes, complements it without stealing the show — the standard opening pairing in Friulian restaurants.

🧀 Frico (cheese and potato cake)

A traditional Friulian farmhouse dish, rich and caramelised with Montasio cheese. Ribolla Gialla, fresh and high in acid, cuts through the fat — or choose a mineral orange-wine Ribolla; an oxidative Friulian white with frico is the region's most authentic match.

🐟 Brodetto di Trieste (Trieste fish stew)

An Adriatic seafood soup with tomato and vinegar acidity. Verduzzo, with moderate acidity and floral notes, or a crisp Pinot Grigio both balance the savoury seafood and the vinegar.
slides.4.title: 🌊 Liguria & Emilia-Romagna: Coastal Pesto and a Pork Civilisation
slides.4.content:
Liguria's pesto culture is made for Vermentino; Emilia-Romagna's empire of cured pork meets its master in Lambrusco

🌿 Liguria: Trenette al Pesto (Genoese pesto pasta)

Vermentino is the obvious choice — the local wine's natural lemon and herb notes resonate with the basil, pine nuts and garlic of pesto. Pigato (a local strain genetically identical to Vermentino) is the most authentic choice of all. Avoid heavy reds, which smother pesto's delicate aromas.

🥓 Emilia-Romagna: The Charcuterie Trio

Lambrusco (a lightly sparkling red) is the natural partner for Emilian charcuterie — Prosciutto di Parma, Mortadella and Culatello all need a sparkling red to cut the pork fat. The bubbles cleanse the palate and the slightly sweet fruit balances the salty richness — centuries of Emilian table wisdom.

🧀 Parmigiano-Reggiano

Aged Parmigiano is an umami bomb but also strongly salty — and the salt offsets umami's negative effect on wine, making red wine pairings possible. Romagna Sangiovese's high acidity cuts the fat, and Lambrusco's bubbles refresh. Parmigiano aged 24 months or more can even take a lighter Barolo.

🍝 Tortellini in Brodo (meat-filled tortellini in broth)

The soul of Emilian cooking, a clear broth rich with pork flavour. Romagna Albana (formerly Albana di Romagna, Italy's first white DOCG), with its delicate fruit, suits the broth perfectly; or choose a light Lambrusco di Sorbara, whose bubbles don't steal the show.
slides.5.title: 🌺 Lombardy & Veneto: Sparkling Pearls and Ageing Giants
slides.5.content:
Lombardy is famous for Franciacorta sparkling wine; Veneto's Soave, Valpolicella and Prosecco form the backbone of the everyday Italian table. Level 2 takes you beyond the basics of Level 1 into the details of regional pairing.

🥂 Franciacorta (Lombardy)

Cotoletta alla Milanese (Milanese veal cutlet): Franciacorta Brut's fine bubbles cut the fried fat and its high acidity refreshes the palate — Milan's most traditional pairing, showing the cutting power of sparkling wine against fried food.
Risotto alla Milanese (saffron risotto): the soft, creamy mousse of Franciacorta Satèn sets off the precious aroma of saffron.

🍷 Amarone / Soave (Veneto)

Amarone + beef braised in red wine (Brasato all'Amarone): Amarone's full body echoes long-braised beef — a classic pairing around Verona.
Soave Classico + Venetian seafood snacks (cicchetti): Soave's almond and minerality resonate with shellfish, prawns and crab.
Prosecco + aperitivo: Prosecco's fresh fruit with a Spritz, olives and light bites is the Veneto way of life.
slides.6.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.6.points.0: ✓ Alto Adige: Speck with Pinot Grigio (a same-region pairing); beef goulash with Lagrein (a South Tyrolean local match)
slides.6.points.1: ✓ Friuli: Prosciutto di San Daniele with Friulano; frico with high-acid Ribolla Gialla; orange-wine pairings are a Friulian speciality
slides.6.points.2: ✓ Liguria: pesto pasta (trenette al pesto) calls for Vermentino/Pigato — herbs with herbs
slides.6.points.3: ✓ Emilia-Romagna: lightly sparkling Lambrusco is the all-purpose cutter for the charcuterie trio (ham, mortadella, aged cheese)
slides.6.points.4: ✓ Parmigiano's saltiness offsets umami's negative effect, making high-acid reds possible (salt is wine's friend)
slides.6.points.5: ✓ Franciacorta + Milanese cutlet: sparkling wine cutting fried fat is a refined northern Italian pairing formula
slides.6.points.6: ✓ Amarone suits rich stews and cured meats, Soave suits seafood and white meat — both from Veneto, yet the choice still depends on the weight of the dish
slides.6.points.7: ✓ The core logic of northern pairing: Alpine whites cut fat, sparkling wines refresh almost anything, local food finds local wine
slides.7.title: 🧠 Northern Italian Pairing Knowledge Check
slides.7.questions.0.question: Which pairing for South Tyrolean Speck best follows the regional principle?
slides.7.questions.0.options.1: B. Alto Adige Pinot Grigio (white from the same region)
slides.7.questions.0.explanation: "What grows together goes together" — Speck is a traditional Alto Adige cured meat, and the fresh fruit of Pinot Grigio from the same region cuts the smoky fat, the pairing that best follows the regional principle.
slides.7.questions.1.question: Why is Emilia-Romagna's Lambrusco the best match for local charcuterie (ham, mortadella)?
slides.7.questions.1.options.1: B. Its light bubbles cut pork fat while its slightly sweet fruit balances the salty richness
slides.7.questions.1.options.2: C. Its very high tannin binds with protein
slides.7.questions.1.options.3: D. It is the world's most expensive wine
slides.7.questions.1.explanation: Lambrusco's value lies in its bubbles and fruit: the bubbles mechanically cut through pork fat (like the cleansing effect of sparkling water) and the slightly sweet fruit balances the salty richness of prosciutto and mortadella — centuries of shared evolution created this perfect match.
slides.7.questions.2.question: What is the first choice with a Milanese cutlet (cotoletta alla Milanese)?
slides.7.questions.2.explanation: Fried food most needs a high-acid sparkling wine to cut the fat; Franciacorta Brut's fine bubbles and high acidity refresh the palate perfectly — Milan's most traditional pairing. Barolo/Amarone are too full and would overwhelm the fried food, and Moscato's sweetness doesn't suit it.
slides.7.questions.3.question: What is the best match for Friuli's frico (cheese and potato cake)?
slides.7.questions.3.explanation: Frico's Montasio cheese is rich in fat and needs high acidity to cut it. Ribolla Gialla's fresh, high acidity is the best choice, and as a native Friulian grape it embodies the regional principle.
slides.7.questions.4.question: Which of these are correct northern Italian pairings? (Select all that apply)
slides.7.questions.4.options.0: A. Ligurian pesto pasta (trenette al pesto) with Vermentino
slides.7.questions.4.options.1: B. Amarone with light steamed white fish
slides.7.questions.4.options.2: C. Soave Classico with Venetian seafood cicchetti
slides.7.questions.4.options.3: D. Lambrusco with Prosciutto di Parma
slides.7.questions.4.explanation: Vermentino's herbal notes echo pesto; Soave's minerality suits seafood; Lambrusco's bubbles cut the fat of the ham — all three are correct local pairings. Amarone is full and rich and would smother the delicacy of steamed white fish, so that pairing is wrong.

quiz.0.explanation: "What grows together goes together" — Speck is a traditional Alto Adige cured meat, and Pinot Grigio from the same region is the pairing that best follows the regional principle.

quiz.1.options.1: Bubbles cut fat + slightly sweet fruit balances salty richness
quiz.1.explanation: Lambrusco's bubbles cut pork fat and its slightly sweet fruit balances the salty richness — centuries of shared evolution created this perfect match.
quiz.2.question: What is the best match for a Milanese cotoletta?
quiz.2.explanation: Fried food needs a high-acid sparkling wine to cut the fat; Franciacorta Brut is Milan's most traditional pairing.
quiz.3.question: Which wine best suits Ligurian pesto pasta?
quiz.3.explanation: Vermentino's natural herbal aromas resonate with the basil and pine nuts of pesto, and it is a native Ligurian grape.
